subject: Sizing request: long-window dedicated pool for Cloudware.ai POC
messages:
From: Ivan Petrov <ivan@cloudware.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing request: long-window Dedicated pool for POC

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to spin up a dedicated pool for a 6-week POC that exercises a 100k-token window for a multi-turn agent (approx 80MB average prefix per session). We expect 50 concurrent active sessions in peak and ~200 qps of short queries outside of long-context reads. Primary ask: an initial SKU recommendation (GPUs + memory) and an estimate of how quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit) would change the fleet footprint and cost.

Attached is a small context profile export (cloudware_context_profile.csv) showing sequence length percentiles and a sample KV cache growth by session. Can you prioritize latency for long-window reads (p90 token latency target ~80ms), and call out any caveats for fallback to smaller context variants?

Appreciate a ballpark ASAP so procurement can align budgets.

Thanks,
Ivan
Head of Platform
Cloudware.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ivan Petrov <ivan@cloudware.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing request: long-window Dedicated pool for POC

Hi Ivan — great meeting. Quick summary below; Laura I cc'd to help turn this into a concise SKU + pricing note.

Top-level read: for 100k effective context with 50 concurrent active sessions, the dominant constraint is KV cache resident memory (per-replica) and per-session KV bandwidth. Two practical deployment patterns:

- Multi-replica pooled model (recommendation for POC): 3 replicas of A100-class or equivalent (max resident memory + NVLink) with 40-48GB GPU memory each, plus an LRU sharded KV store in CPU/GPU hybrid. This prioritizes bandwidth and latency with room for caching hot prefixes.
- Single larger-instance footprint (higher memory GPUs): 2x 80GB GPUs (for simpler state pinning) to reduce cross-device KV fetching but at higher cost.

Quantization impact (ballpark):
- FP16 / BF16 baseline: highest quality, largest memory.
- 8-bit (INT8 or Q8): reduces model weights memory ~1.8x and KV cache footprint modestly, often allowing 20-30% more sessions per GPU on average depending on KV storage strategy.
- 4-bit (Q4) aggressive: reduces weights further (~3x) but increases decoding latency risk if kernel paths are not fully optimized for long KV lookups; expect improved capacity but must validate quality/regressions.

I pulled rough math into an initial calc sheet (gpu_sku_calc_v1.xlsx). Laura, can you take Ivan's profile and my notes and produce a short SKU recommendation (replica count, GPU family, expected unit monthly cost for POC) and a short appendix on operational caveats?

Action items:
1) Laura to produce SKU + cost note.
2) Karthik / Prio to validate quantized kernel availability for the target model and long-KV scenario.
3) Ivan to confirm whether fallback to 32k/8k context variants is acceptable for degraded latency cases.

Thanks — I can push an annotated plan by EOD.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing request: long-window Dedicated pool for POC

Ivan — attached is a concise SKU recommendation and cost estimate (gpu_sku_calc_v1.xlsx). Summary below: 

Summary recommendation (POC, performance-first):
- Start with a 3x-replica pool using NVIDIA H100-80GB (or equivalent) with NVLink-enabled nodes. Rationale: high resident memory for KV cache, strong inter-GPU bandwidth for pinned prefixes.
- Provision 1x medium CPU KV node per 6 GPUs to serve cold KV fetches and maintain <80ms p90 for token read paths.
- Storage: ephemeral NVMe for warm caching; we recommend prefix-level persistent storage for rehydration between sessions.

Expected POC sizing numbers (ballpark):
- 3 replicas * H100-80GB = 3 GPUs (replicated capacity); with 8-bit quantization we estimate the pool covers ~65 concurrent long-window sessions at target latency, with headroom for burst.
- If Cloudware insists on 50 concurrent sessions as a hard SL, 3 replicas should be safe with 8-bit; FP16 gives less headroom and higher infra cost.

Quantization caveats:
- 8-bit: recommended for POC. Best balance of cost and quality; requires validation against your eval prompts. Expect 20-35% reduction in GPU memory usage across weights and some KV metadata.
- 4-bit: only advisable after a focused quality/regression run. Kernel maturity for 4-bit long-KV workflows is mixed; we can run a controlled test.

Operational notes:
- Canary a smaller context fallback route (32k) for low-cost fallbacks when KV hit rate drops.
- Implement cache warming for known high-value sessions to keep p95 below 120ms when under heavy load.

Attachments: GPU calc workbook and a short quantization note (redwood_quant_notes_v1.pdf). Marcus / Karthik: please review the numbers in the sheet; I left a few conservative buffers.

Next steps:
- Karthik validate kernel support and share any potential performance risks.
- Marcus to confirm cost/contract language we can present to procurement.

Laura Bennett
Manager, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing request: long-window Dedicated pool for POC

Laura / Marcus — I ran the early microbenchmarks against our Q8 and Q4 kernels with a synthetic KV access pattern similar to Ivan's profile. Notes: 

- Q8 (8-bit) paths are stable on H100 and A100 with our continuous-batching runtime; latency increase vs FP16 is negligible for the decoding path, KV fetchs dominate. Memory usage decreases ~25-30% depending on tensor packing.
- Q4 (4-bit) reduces resident model memory ~2.5-3x but we see a 10-18% increase in token decode tail latency when KV misses require cross-device fetches; this is due to less mature fused-kernel coverage for certain attention/block layouts.
- Most important: KV cache placement strategy matters more than raw model precision. If we can pin hot prefixes on-GPU (sharded by session affinity), Q4 looks attractive. If we have frequent cross-device cold fetches, Q4 penalizes latency.

I recommend:
1) POC: default to Q8 quantization on H100-80GB, tune tensor packing for your model.
2) Run a short Q4 regression for 24 hours on a scaled-down replica (1 node) with your real prompts to check quality and decode latency tails.
3) Implement KV hot-set pinning and an LRU eviction policy; measure warm-hit ratio and simulate fallback to 32k contexts.

I updated the calc sheet with microbenchmarks numbers in the perf tab. Prio, Marcus — happy to join a call with Ivan to walk these tradeoffs.

- Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference R&D
Redwood Inference

Appreciate if you can send this by EOD today so procurement can include in the purchase request.

Ivan

Ivan — attached is the single-line SKU and monthly POC estimate pulled from the spreadsheet. Summary here: 

SKU recommendation (POC, performance-first):
- 3x H100-80GB replicas (1 GPU per replica) + 1x medium CPU KV node (6U CPU with NVMe).
- Default quantization: Q8 (8-bit) with an optional Q4 upgrade path after validation.

Estimated monthly run rate (POC, quoted):
- GPU capacity (3x H100-80GB): $42,000/mo (unitized hosting + support).
- CPU KV node + NVMe + networking: $5,200/mo.
- One-time onboarding + canary testing fee: $6,500 (includes two model validation runs and small dataset evals).
- Total monthly (recurring): $47,200/mo.

Fallback runbook (short):
- If KV warm-hit ratio < 45% for >15 minutes -> trigger cache-warm job and scale-to-warm (temporary additional CPU KV shards).
- If decode p95 token latency > 150ms for >5 minutes -> apply 32k fallback route for new sessions and throttle background rehydration.
- If error rate for long-window fetches > 0.8% for >10 minutes -> auto-failover to smaller-segment replicas and notify oncall.

Deliverables sent: single-line SKU + cost sheet (gpu_sku_calc_v1.xlsx), quantization notes (redwood_quant_notes_v1.pdf). Laura will open a formal quote and contract language. Karthik / Priyom will help with the Q4 regression plan if you want to try upgrading after POC.

Next steps:
- Marcus to drop formal quote and SOW by 2027-04-26.
- Cloudware to confirm purchase intent and preferred billing cadence.

Thanks everyone — happy to jump on a short call to walk procurement through the numbers.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
